sentences.text: From FY2016 to FY2025 net interest income compounded at 4.0% [F115], ahead of noninterest income at 2.8% [F116] and net income at 2.8% [F117].
Net income fell 28.3% to $4.96 billion in FY2020 [D99][F25].
Net income then rose 60.6% to $7.96 billion in FY2021 [D125][F26], reflecting a lower provision for credit losses [P57].
Net interest income rose 17.9% in FY2022 [D159], primarily on rising interest rates on earning assets and strong loan growth [P44].
Noninterest expense rose 26.6% in FY2023 [D188], reflecting MUB acquisition charges and a $734 million FDIC special assessment [P30].
Payment Services added 1.4pp to FY2025 revenue growth [D261] and made up 25.8% of revenue [D259].
Its revenue grew 5.4% [D260], driven by merchant processing and card revenue on higher sales volume [P4].
Consumer and Business Banking subtracted 1.3pp [D253], as net interest income fell on deposit mix and second-quarter loan sales [P6].
Bank revenue grew 4.4% in FY2025 [D239] while noninterest expense fell 2.0% [D238], lifting net income 20.2% [D227].
Diluted shares fell from 1,724 million in FY2016 [X66] to 1,558 million in FY2025 [X75], so EPS compounded at 4.0% [F119] against net income at 2.8% [F117].
The efficiency ratio was 59.0% in FY2025 [D220], near the window median of 59.3% [D277], between a low of 55.3% [D275] and a high of 67.4% [D276].
The ratio fell 3.9pp from 62.9% in FY2024 [D195] to 59.0% [D220], as prior-year merger charges and the FDIC special assessment dropped out [P10].
The largest move was FY2023, when the ratio rose 5.8pp from 61.6% [D144] to 67.4% [D170], on MUB integration costs and the FDIC charge [P30].
Provision for credit losses was 7.7% of revenue in FY2025 [D221], above the four-bank peer median of 6.1% [D285].
The provision fell 2.3% to $2.19 billion [X145], driven by improved credit quality and loan sales [P12].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank, so capital return against net income is used instead.
Buybacks plus dividends were $3.66 billion in FY2025 [D218], 48.3% of net income of $7.57 billion [F30].
In FY2019 the payout was $6.97 billion [D65] against net income of $6.91 billion [F24], about 100.8%.
Shareholders' equity rose 11.3% to $65.2 billion in FY2025 [D233][F114].
Return on average equity was 12.2% [D226], above the peer median of 11.8% [D283], at the 71st percentile of seven banks [D282].
Loans were 73.5% of deposits [D224], up from 67.2% in FY2021 [D122], while cash fell 17.0% to $46.9 billion [D232][F97].
Buybacks were $489 million in FY2025 [X85] against $4.53 billion in FY2019 [X79], and diluted shares moved -0.2% to 1,558 million [D237][X75].
Bank revenue fell 2.4% to $27.3 billion in FY2024 [D194][D214] on deposit mix and pricing pressure on net interest income [P20], then recovered 4.4% in FY2025 [D239].
Consumer and Business Banking revenue fell 3.9% in FY2025 [D252] to $8.87 billion [S57], from $10.3 billion in FY2023 [S55].
Segment net income was $1.72 billion [S7] against $2.50 billion in FY2023 [S5], and the latest revenue decline reflects deposit mix and loan sales [P6].
Provision at 7.7% of revenue [D221] exceeds the four-bank peer median of 6.1% [D285], with the allowance at 2.0% of loans [D225].
Data gap: long-term debt is reported only through FY2022 [F104], so net debt and leverage trends cannot be assessed.
An efficiency ratio above the window median of 59.3% [D277], from 59.0% in FY2025 [D220], would reverse the cost improvement; look in the FY2026 10-K.
A net interest margin below 2.70%, the FY2024 level [P15], from 2.72% in FY2025 [P15], would reverse the net interest income recovery; look in the FY2026 10-K.
Consumer and Business Banking revenue below FY2025's $8.87 billion [S57] would extend the segment decline; look in the FY2026 10-K.
